authored.note: Written for learners from the sources named in each block. It is an explanation, not a recording. Facts listed under each block are checked word for word against those sources.

summary.text: A tool permission answers "may this tool be called?" It does not answer "is the agent doing the job it was actually given?" In this lab an agent is allowed to use the lookup_policy tool, yet an untrusted instruction steers it into using that tool for a different, unauthorized job. The lesson: an authorized tool is not an authorized goal.
facts: This lab teaches one idea: an authorized tool is not an authorized goal.
lookup_policy can be granted and still be the wrong use of that tool.

glance.label: What the attacker wants
glance.text: The attacker wants the granted lookup_policy tool used for a task the server never authorized.
facts: The attacker wants granted lookup_policy used for a task the server never authorized.

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: Only the text of one untrusted instruction in the lab's closed fixture. The browser cannot choose the setting, the grants, the instruction body or the goal decision.
facts: The browser does not choose profile, grants, instruction body, or goal decision.

glance.label: Where it gets in
glance.text: An untrusted instruction arrives alongside the real task and proposes a change to it. Here it proposes extract_full_policy in place of summarizing the lending policy.
facts: Untrusted instruction may propose a change. It cannot redefine the server-owned task.

glance.label: Where the trust boundary is
glance.text: Between the proposed goal and the effective task. The server-owned task is authoritative; the goal-integrity control decides what the effective task becomes, and only then is the tool checked.
facts: AUTHORITATIVE TASK → UNTRUSTED INSTRUCTION → PROPOSED GOAL → CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 → EFFECTIVE TASK → CTRL-MCP-001 → AUTHORIZED TOOL → HANDLER.

glance.label: Two controls, two questions
glance.text: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 asks whether the task is still the authorized one. CTRL-MCP-001 asks whether the tool is granted. They solve different problems, and a goal DENY is not a tool DENY.
facts: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 protects the task boundary. CTRL-MCP-001 at acmebank.mcp.authorize is the tool PDP. These solve different problems.

glance.label: Authorized tool, unauthorized use
glance.text: On the vulnerable ATTACK setting the granted tool ran for the expanded goal. On the defended RETEST the goal control denied the expansion and the tool still ran for the original task. The lab does not say the tool was compromised or that the tool check failed.
facts: Do not claim the tool itself was compromised. Do not claim the MCP grant check failed.
That is not universal prompt-injection bypass.

glance.label: What evidence exists
glance.text: Each run records the proposed and the effective action, both decisions, and handler counts split into in-task and wrong-goal. The handler counts are the authoritative record of what ran; Splunk only corroborates them.
facts: Runtime handler counts are authoritative. Splunk completeness is corroboration.

path.label: Untrusted instruction
path.detail: Text that proposes a different task.
path.fact: AUTHORITATIVE TASK → UNTRUSTED INSTRUCTION → PROPOSED GOAL

path.label: Task boundary
path.fact: It cannot redefine the server-owned task.

path.label: Goal decision
path.detail: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 decides what the effective task becomes.

outcomes.label: DENY (defended retest)
outcomes.detail: unauthorized_task_expansion; the effective task stays the authorized one.

outcomes.label: OBSERVE (vulnerable attack setting)
outcomes.detail: A labelled lab-only fail-open overlay; the expansion goes through.

path.label: Tool authorization
path.detail: CTRL-MCP-001 allowed lookup_policy on both the attack and the retest.

path.label: Handler
path.detail: lookup_policy runs; the in-task and wrong-goal counts say for which purpose.
path.fact: Wrong-goal handler count 0 is the authoritative non-execution evidence for the prohibited action.

path.label: Evidence copy
path.detail: A copy of the telemetry goes to Splunk, which only observes.
path.fact: Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY a tool or a task.

known.text: extract_full_policy is not an MCP tool. It labels lookup_policy as wrong-goal vs in-task.
facts: extract_full_policy is not an MCP tool. It labels lookup_policy as wrong-goal vs in-task.

known.text: RETEST is not MCP DENY. MCP ALLOW on RETEST is expected.
facts: RETEST is not MCP DENY. MCP ALLOW on RETEST is expected.

known.text: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 evaluates task/goal integrity. It is not a tool PDP.
facts: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 evaluates task/goal integrity. It is not a tool PDP.

known.text: Missing Splunk event is not prevention.
facts: Missing Splunk event is not prevention.

known.text: CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
facts: CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.

terms.text: The tool being granted says nothing about whether it is being used for the job the server authorized.
The proposed action is what the instruction asked for. The effective action is what the system actually continued with after the goal decision.
A goal DENY refuses the changed task. It is a different decision from the tool check, which still allows lookup_policy.
The lab separates what you read into five planes so that none is mistaken for another.
terms.fact: Five planes: TASK, INSTRUCTION, GOAL DECISION, TOOL AUTHORIZATION, EXECUTION.

terms.text: The identifier that ties every event of one experiment together. Every launch gets a new one.

defender.text: Keep the task on the server. An untrusted instruction may propose a change, and the goal control must deny an unauthorized expansion while the legitimate tool use carries on. Blocking the tool is not the defense.
facts: Untrusted instruction may propose a change. It cannot redefine the server-owned task.
DEFENSE DOES NOT MEAN block lookup_policy.

lines: Do not label SAFE, TRUSTED, APPROVED, or BENIGN.
Do not claim the tool itself was compromised.
Do not claim the MCP grant check failed.
Do not say MCP blocked the attack.
